text:
Maya (Product): afternoon check — quick status for the release window at 3pm PT.
Maya (Product): what I did: finalized spec updates for routing fallback, merged small UX copy fixes.
Maya (Product): blockers: still need signoff on the fallback matrix (spec section 2.2) and a quick smoke on canary config.
Maya (Product): today: get signoff, trigger canary, confirm telemetry dashboards show expected traffic.

Tom (Eng): on it — i'll review the spec now, should be a 20–30m pass. ping me on the PR when ready: https://git.internal/r/redwood/repo/pull/4123
Tom (Eng): for canary, i've prepared a short script to restrict traffic to 5% for 30m:
```
# canary restrict
k run canary-roll --percent=5 --duration=30m
```
Tom (Eng): will queue that at 2:50p so dashboards have time to warm up.

Anika (Eng-ML): FYI the model fallback branch requires a small param rename: `enable_model_fallback` -> `model_fallback_mode` or the deploy config parser rejects it. I left a comment on config.md.
Anika (Eng-ML): also doing a quick eval run against the smoke prompts to ensure no quality regression, ETA ~15m.

Jae (Eng Manager): thanks team. Can someone confirm SLA implications if fallback triggers? we discussed 99.9 -> 99.5 tradeoffs in last meeting, want to call out in release notes.

Maya (Product): good catch, Jae. I'm updating the release notes with the explicit SLA change and user-visible behavior. i'll add a short Q&A in the notes about when fallback will be triggered.

Tom (Eng): SLA: if fallback triggers, latency SLO preserved but throughput may decrease; note in notes that Dedicated customers get override to not fallback (policy flag).

Anika (Eng-ML): smoke eval passed for top-50 prompts, diff looks clean. attaching quick summary in thread: precision drop 0.1% on one prompt group. not blocking for rollout but logging a regression ticket.

Maya (Product): thanks — file the regression ticket and link it in the release notes (ticket #927).

deploy-bot: scheduled canary job `canary-roll` at 2026-03-17T14:50:00Z, target 5% for 30m. Job id: cb-20260317-77.

Tom (Eng): kicked off the canary, monitoring cloudwatch and internal dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/release/1767
Tom (Eng): small nit — Anika, can you confirm the eval dataset included the new routing prompt variants?

Anika (Eng-ML): included them yes, added two new prompts for routing-edge-cases. all green.

Jae (Eng Manager): can we do a quick rollback plan in case KV cache invalidation occurs? what's the manual path?

Tom (Eng): rollback steps: 1) scale canary down to 0% with `k run canary-roll --percent=0`, 2) revert config to tagged commit `v2026-03-17-rc1`, 3) flush prefix cache: `redis-cli -h cache.my flushdb` (we do this during low traffic).
Tom (Eng): i'll paste these into the ops runbook after the canary finishes.

Maya (Product): final ask — can someone do a quick CR for the release notes language? short, action-oriented. I put a draft at https://docs.internal/redwood/releases/2026-03-17-draft.md

Jae (Eng Manager): i'll review release notes in 10m.

Tom (Eng): reviewed and left a tiny wording suggestion. :thumbsup:

Anika (Eng-ML): +1 on notes. no blockers from ML side.

Maya (Product): perfect. thanks all — i'll mark this thread as done once canary completes and dashboards are green. :party_parrot:

deploy-bot: canary `cb-20260317-77` completed at 2026-03-17T15:20:00Z, status: success.

Maya (Product): canary success — closing out. follow-ups: ticket #927 (regression), add ops rollback steps to runbook, final publish of release notes after Jae's review.

Jae (Eng Manager): good job team.

Tom (Eng): thanks everyone.
